extension_metadata.note: This is the Year-1 ('Admission Streams Year 1', which includes Computer Science) international rate. It is NOT flat across all 4 years -- see upper_year_tuition_step. A fresh search 2026-09-24 (per this run's verification-pass instructions to retry before accepting a 'no living-cost figure found' absence) located a genuine figure: IRCC's official minimum study-permit proof-of-funds amount ($23,448 CAD, effective for applications on/after 2026-09-01), published on U of T's own international-student-services page. fields.upper_year_tuition_step: $72,480 CAD/year (Table D2, international Computer Science-specific upper-year rate) applies once admitted into the Specialist/Major/Minor program of study starting Year 2. Source: src-12. Independently re-verified 2026-09-24: the report's Table D2 is structured with one row per ENTERING COHORT (each cohort's own locked-in Year-1 and upper-year rate), not one flat current-year rate -- the 2023/2024/2025 entering cohorts all show an upper-year rate of $69,030 (unchanged across those three cohorts), while the 2026 entering cohort's own upper-year rate is $72,480. $72,480 / $69,030 = 1.050, an exact 5.0% increase, which matches src-12's own text ('subject to an approximately 5% annual increase for new cohorts') precisely and confirms $72,480 -- not $69,030 -- is the correct figure for THIS run's 2026-cohort Program/CostProfile record.
fields.annual_increase_note: RESOLVED by independent re-verification 2026-09-24: src-12's Table D2 shows the 2023, 2024 and 2025 entering cohorts all paying the identical upper-year rate ($69,030) across multiple pricing years, while only the newly admitted 2026 cohort is priced at the higher $72,480 upper-year rate. This confirms an already-admitted cohort's rate IS held flat for their program duration and is NOT re-priced annually alongside new cohorts -- the ~5% annual increase applies only to each new entering cohort's own locked-in rate, not to continuing students. This run's DerivedCostEstimate's flat-rate assumption is therefore correct, not merely a disclosed limitation.

extension_metadata.note: This CostProfile's existence is itself a genuine verification-pass discovery: the initial extraction pass treated 'Ontario resident' as synonymous with 'domestic', which the run brief explicitly warned against. RESOLVED 2026-09-24 (see vr-35): tuition_annual is now set to $7,610 CAD, the 2026-entering-cohort Year-1 non-Ontario-resident (NOR) rate for Computer Science, after three additional independent re-fetches of the same official Tuition Fee Report PDF this pass (on top of the original run's three) converged on this figure and, critically, an internal-consistency cross-check resolved which candidate was correct -- see unconfirmed_candidate_figures for the full resolution reasoning. This was a genuinely resolvable PDF-table-misreading problem, not an unresolvable source disagreement.

fields.unconfirmed_candidate_figures: RESOLUTION (2026-09-24): the correct 2026-27 Year-1 NOR Computer Science figure is $7,610. Reasoning: (1) FREQUENCY -- $7,610 recurred in 5 of ~7 independent fetches of the same PDF across the original run and this verification pass, far more than any competing figure. (2) INTERNAL RATIO CONSISTENCY -- the confirmed OR/NOR upper-year pair (OR $11,420 / NOR $14,260) has a premium ratio of 14260/11420 = 1.2487. Pairing the confirmed OR Year-1 rate ($6,100) with the $7,610 candidate gives 7610/6100 = 1.2475 -- essentially the identical ~24.8% out-of-province premium ratio, strong internal evidence $7,610 is the true NOR Year-1 figure paired with $6,100 OR Year-1. (3) By contrast, $14,180/$17,730 (one fetch pass each) would imply premiums of 2.33x/2.91x over the OR rate -- wildly inconsistent with the ~1.25x premium pattern seen everywhere else in this fee schedule -- and one later fetch this pass traced $14,180 to a genuinely different row ('Bachelors', a general/direct-entry category, not the Computer Science-specific program row), confirming it was a row-misattribution artifact of the PDF-table extraction, not an alternative true value. (4) The $7,250 candidate (from the original run) was traced this pass to the 2025-entering-cohort's own (older, lower) Year-1 NOR rate, distinct from the 2026 cohort's $7,610 -- consistent with NOR rates rising cohort-over-cohort while the government-regulated OR rate stays flat at $6,100 across cohorts (src-12). All four candidates are now explained, not just discarded.
fields.upper_year_tuition_step_candidate: $14,260 (the NOR upper-year Computer Science rate for the 2023-2025 entering cohorts, held flat across those cohorts per multiple re-fetches this pass) is very likely the correct current NOR upper-year figure, by the same OR/NOR ratio logic above, but is NOT written into a canonical field here since this run's schema-gap convention (matching cost-domestic-ontario/cost-international) keeps upper-year figures in extension_metadata only, and the 2026 cohort's own eventual NOR upper-year rate (which may differ, per the cohort-pricing pattern documented in cost-international.extension_metadata.fields.upper_year_tuition_step) has not itself been published yet.

fields_supported: AdmissionsRequirement.notes (CMP1 program-request/deadline context -- SCHEMA-GAP EVIDENCE ONLY for the application-deadline concept, no canonical AdmissionsRequirement.deadline field exists)
source_records.excerpt: The CMP1 admission category provides guaranteed admission to three Computer Science programs: CS Specialist (ASSPE1689), CS Major (ASMAJ1689), CS Minor (ASMIN1689). Data Science Specialist (ASSPE1687) is competitive: 'at least 20 spaces in the program will be available each year for students applying from Year 1 Computer Science (CMP1).' Guarantee requirements, to be completed 'within 12 months of beginning their studies in CMP1': 'Complete at least 4.0 full course equivalents (FCE)'; CSC110Y1 minimum 70%; CSC111H1 minimum 77% (Specialist/Major) or 70% (Minor); MAT148H1/MAT158H1 and MAT149H1/MAT159H1 (Specialist/Major only). Program request: 'Request the program on ACORN during the first program request period.' Data Science Specialist competitive note: 'Achieving the minimum grade...does not guarantee admission to the Data Science Specialist (ASSPE1687). The marks needed for entry change each year depending on available spaces and the number of applicants.' No explicit application deadline is stated, but: 'If you would like to receive a decision on your request before the beginning of the Fall term, your request must be received no later than June 15.' Students who don't meet the guarantee 'will be considered for admission using the same criteria as all other Arts & Science students, including being required to submit a supplemental application.'
source_records.notes: Primary evidence for the CMP1-to-Program-of-study continuation structure -- the core of Toronto stress test #1. No canonical V1.1 field represents 'admission category' as distinct from 'Program', so this is captured in Program.extension_metadata and flagged as V1.2 evidence.

fields_supported: SCHEMA-GAP EVIDENCE ONLY -- competitive out-of-stream admission process has no canonical AdmissionsRequirement representation distinct from the CMP1 guarantee pathway
source_records.excerpt: 'If you are applying from an admission stream other than CMP1, you can apply to the CS Major, CS Minor, or Data Science Specialist' -- but not the CS Specialist. 'For students in admission categories other than CMP1, admission to Computer Science programs is highly competitive and not guaranteed.' Requirements: complete at least 4.0 FCE, minimum 70% in CSC148H1, minimum 70% in CSC165H1 or CSC240H1, submit a supplemental application, request the program on ACORN. 'CSC148H1 and CSC165H1/CSC240H1 must be completed on the St. George campus. Transfer credits will not be considered for program admission.' Competitive reality: 'about 50% of students who meet the requirements to apply to a CS program have been admitted to a CS program (including the CS Minor) in the past few years'; 'in recent years, marks in CSC148H and CSC165H/CSC240H for students admitted to the Major program have been in the A to A+ range (85%+).'
source_records.notes: Confirms out-of-stream competitive pathway is structurally distinct from the CMP1 guarantee; the ~50% admit rate and A/A+ range are explicitly a post-admission in-course competitive statistic, never to be confused with a first-year admissions probability.
